AI Search / GEO.what_happened: AI is killing SEO traffic is not completely wrong, but definitely not completely right. I a new analysis of Similarweb…

sources.name: Kevin_Indig
sources.excerpt: AI is killing SEO traffic is not completely wrong, but definitely not completely right. I a new analysis of Similarweb data (10k domains, US + France, 3 years), I found Organic Search fell -13.2% in the US and 24.4% in France over the last 2 years. HOWEVER, not all of that is due to AI (Overviews). Paid Search has grown strongly over the same time horizon, probably due to more real estate in the SERPs and harder differentiation from organic results. Also, organic traffic losses are more concentrated in industries like publishing, which lost lost 41.5% in the US and 42.5% in France over the last 2 years. Lastly, Google's updates are aggressive and often reduce rank performance that can be,…
sources.author: @Kevin_Indig

AI Search / GEO.what_happened: Fascinating example of how Google can “play dumb” with rank trackers – as a companion to poisoned search results…

sources.name: brodieseo
sources.excerpt: Fascinating example of how Google can “play dumb” with rank trackers – as a companion to poisoned search results. Search “easy strawberry jam”, and the standard organic results can focus on Easy, the TV series, even while Google’s AI overview gives you a jam recipe. New research from @nozzleio found this pattern spiked sharply: in the week of Sept. 28, it appeared on 25% of the study’s page 1 or page 2 SERPs, peaking at 39.9% on a single day. It’s a different issue from the poisoned SERPs issue, but another reason to check the actual results before treating a sudden rank-tracker drop as a Google update. Google is certainly trying to make it as difficult as possible for rank trackers and…
sources.author: @brodieseo
